newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU set to fine five ferry operators - sources.
newsitem.headline: EU set to fine five ferry operators - sources.

text.p: The European Commission is expected on Wednesday to fine five ferry companies for allegedly operating a price cartel in 1992, European Union sources said.
The EU executive was due to impose penalties on the ferry operations of Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co, Stena-Sealink, Brittany Ferries, Sea France and North Sea Ferries.
The fines were not expected to be substantial, however, as the alleged cartel did not last long.
One source said they would total less than one million European currency units ($1.26 million).

The Wall Street Journal said on Monday EU anti-trust investigators had found that the companies agreed to impose a surcharge on cross-channel freight shipments in 1992 to compensate for the effects of the devaluation of the British pound.
The Commission launched an inquiry following a complaint from freight companies about the surcharge.
The Commission can impose fines rising to 10 percent of turnover.
